title: Quiver representations, path algebras, and Gabriel’s theorem, Part II: multisegment duality
summary: Starting from finite type-A interval classification, this roadmap constructs integer graded nilpotent pairs and opposite-degree commuting operators over the complex numbers. Generic ranks produce multisegment duality; admissible images give ramified truncation. Weighted inclusion chains and monotone grid paths compute adjacent dual counts and prove additivity for the canonical maximal split. The resulting operations supply general-linear newform comparisons and unipotent induction through the existing representation-theoretic classification interface.
readme: Integer intervals keep their full multiplicities. VN raises degree, WL lowers degree, and a shift by c has V(c)_a=V_(a−c). The polynomial Zariski topology is separate from the usual topology of C. Parent QuiverRepresentations Layers 1,2,5 provide interval classification. The elementary adjacent rank formula is proved by block coordinates, finite chain decomposition and path weights. Representation classification and general Aubert duality remain existing-owner inputs. Every stage is planned, with the exact geometric and representation interface gaps recorded in the packet.

stages.title: Integer multisegments and maximal peeling
stages.description: Adapt the parent’s finite type-A interval carrier to integer endpoints and finite multisets. Pin inclusive endpoints, singleton deletion under right truncation, degree dimensions and total length. Construct the multisegment of distinct inclusion-maximal intervals, taking one copy of each, and its multiplicity-sensitive remainder.

stages.title: Graded operators, shifts and images
stages.description: Model finite support integer graded complex vector spaces and degree +1 VN / degree −1 WL operators. Compare with finite type-A representations and reverse orientation. Construct standard interval blocks, graded isomorphisms, shifts and actual image pairs; prove the truncation/image dictionary and reconstruction from graded dimension and the unshifted VN image.

stages.title: Centralizers and generic multisegment duality
stages.description: Construct the opposite-degree commuting subspaces. Prove the block coefficient parameterization and both image restriction surjectivity statements. Put the polynomial Zariski topology on finite dimensional coordinate spaces and derive a simultaneous maximal-rank open locus. Plan the finite-orbit conormal symmetry input explicitly and use it to prove generic commuting duality is involutive. The geometric dimension/constructibility bridge is an identified gap, not a generic black box.

stages.title: Admissible images and ramified truncation
stages.description: Construct admissible commuting triples and the induced VN operator on Im L. Prove Lemma 3.4’s dense open image-admissible locus, then simultaneous genericity for restrictions of the same L on every iterated Im N. Define ram(m)=dual(truncate(dual(m))) and identify it with the VN type on Im L. Prove that ram and right truncation commute, keeping the VN shift −1 explicit.

stages.title: Weighted chains and adjacent ranks
stages.description: Construct the full cut submultisegment meeting [a,a+1], the weighted inclusion-chain maximum, and the occurrence endpoint poset. Prove finite Dilworth and matching rank in this special matrix pattern. Construct monotone grid paths from (a+1,a) to (1,r); show their maximum weight is the chain maximum and prove the adjacent Knight–Zelevinsky formula: dual intervals containing [a,a+1] have count Card(m_a)−E_a(m). No formula for higher powers is assumed.

stages.title: Maximal split and newform interfaces
stages.description: Prove right truncation commutes with maximal peeling, prove the weighted chain decrement, and deduce Proposition 2.7 only for the canonical maximal split. Check repeated intervals and the rank-17 source example. Export the ramified multisegment and split identity to the general-linear newform and unipotent-induction consumers. Import the representation-theoretic identification with Zelevinsky duality from early ET.6 classification, reconciled with current upstream smooth-representation targets; its pinned carrier/signature is an explicit interface gap.
